Black Ops 7 is a *fun* game, however there are plenty of glaring issues, plenty stemming from the beta. 

The "Campaign" is not even a Campaign, it is a glorified Warzone contract for the majority of the missions, with a couple of linear sections which are awful. It is a crime to call this a sequel to the Black Ops 2 Campaign, Black Ops 3  somehow does a better job at that. Endgame, however, is fun and that should've replaced Campaign, period. 

Multiplayer is one of the better launch experiences of the mode in the Warzone era of COD, to an extent. The launch maps are surprisingly good, with a couple of exceptions and the matchmaking is a breath of fresh air. However, Treyarch's refusal to make the mode a "fair" and balanced experience is draining. After years of aim assist complaints they finally nerf it, to go back on that a week after launch, despite aim assist being in a good spot post nerf. The overall Create a Class balancing is one of the worst I have ever seen in a COD game, up there with MW2. The game is heavily AR dominated, even after the recent nerfs. With SMG's being borderline useless with their insanely high recoil and lower damage ranges, with aim assist and AR's running rampant, it makes using an SMG miserable. The Akita Shotgun and Warden 308 Marksman Rifle are also up there being zero skill cheese.

There is plenty of bs free kill items for the lower skilled players like Drone Pods, and the Red/Blue perk hybrid, Scout, which completely hides you off the enemies mini map. There is zero reason why you should be completely hidden from the mini map, including shooting an unsuppressed weapon and enemy HARP's, just because you got 1 single kill. On top of those, COD is still suffering from the lack of the Pick 10 system in Create a Class, which leads to the majority of lobbies being a lethal/tactical spam, which can be replenished by Scavenger. Why, Treyarch? 
 
On top of the HARP being countered by bs, it is the weakest type of Advanced UAV streak COD has ever seen, being able to be destroyed with 5 rockets. The majority of streaks in BO7 are on the better side compared to recent years, though. 

Thanks to the game being available on PC Game Pass, there is an influx of cheaters, more than I have ever seen in the launch period of a COD game in the past 6 years. The requirement for Secure Boot and TPM 2.0 was pointless and Ricochet continues to be a marketing ploy more than anything.

The Networking is also atrocious in Multiplayer, plenty of server disconnections and desync. But, "ping is king" according to ATVI

There isn't too much bad about Zombies, it is a BO6 DLC and feels very similar, but it is still great fun. The return of Survival mode is nice to see, and Treyarch seem to plan to support it post launch too, which is great, depending on how long  that support is kept. Cursed mode, which is a modernised version of classic Zombies in a sense, is a nice addition to the mode, which has "Relics" to unlock to make the mode harder and exclusive rewards, like new Pack a Punch camos. 

The launch Zombies map, Ashes of the Damned, is great, especially for modern Zombies standards. The best way to describe it is a modern take on TranZit.  It seems like Zombies is finally going back to not being grounded and taking itself too seriously, thanks to the story taking place in the Dark Aether. However, I am afraid that this game will follow BO6 with the launch map(s) and DLC1 being strong, and then quality dropping off later in the year. For that reason alone, I cannot recommend someone to buy the game strictly for Zombies as of right now. 

The upcoming Season 1 content for both Multiplayer and Zombies does look promising, with an excess of maps in Multiplayer and an interesting looking Zombies map. If Treyarch keeps up that level of support throughout the post launch content updates, then the game will be in for a good year.  As of right now in the launch period I cannot recommend a game that is a glorified BO6 DLC, (but a better game) even though I am the biggest COD meatrider. The game is enjoyable and I will continue to play it, but it is not worth the $70 price tag, if you are looking to buy this game, please wait until Season 2-3 or try it out on Game Pass.

This is a hard game to review, as its quality varies significantly between each mode. I'm mostly a zombies player, so that will be the focus. The campaign is not as bad as the online discourse makes it appear, but isn't good either. It's somehow both a weird fever dream and quite bland, leaving a mess struggling to find its identity. The inability to pause in solo and lack of AI allies doesn't help. The multiplayer is a nice improvement over Black Ops 6, but not enough to justify the high price on its own. The campaign is a 5.5/10 and multiplayer is a 7/10.

Zombies is, in my opinion, the best part of Black Ops 7. Treyarch has addressed most of the shortcomings of last year's zombies. This includes removing special/elite enemy spam, adding actual atmosphere, rebalancing some augments, buffing weapons, and bringing back the classic points system in cursed mode. Ashes of the Damned is a great launch map and I'm excited for what's next. That being said, zombies is pretty similar to last year and feels like what Black Ops 6 should have been. Zombies is an 8/10 and the overall game is a 7/10. I do recommend the game if you're a die hard COD/Black Ops fan, especially for zombies, but I'd recommend buying on sale.

Black Ops 7 is a fast and energetic shooter that shines in its online modes. The new movement options feel smooth and create exciting fights. The online action is the strongest part of the game and can be a lot of fun with friends.

The story mode is less impressive. It feels rushed and does not reach the emotional level of earlier titles. It works better as a simple action experience than as a deep campaign.

The game has technical problems at times, yet the core action is enjoyable. If you enjoy quick matches and team play, this game can be worth your time. If you want a strong story, it may feel weaker.

Overall it is a fun but uneven entry that delivers great action and a weaker campaign.

I'll go against the grain a bit here. I wish I had a "Neutral" option, to be honest, OR at least a 5 fraction ratio, but I'll say a few things about this game.

First of all, yes. [b]The campaign is terrible.[/b] Without spoiling, all I can say is that [b]it feels a bit like a Resident Evil campaign where you're under some sort of psychological spell the entire time.[/b] It feels like Treyarch/Raven [i]wanted to make a horror game campaign, but since they're stuck making Call of Duty, they had to shoehorn it in there.[/i] Which sucks, cause I did actually like the Black Ops 6 campaign (played the game exclusively through Game Pass, until they screwed with it). So I don't recommend playing it. And if you want to do the Campaign camo grind, do it on Endgame since it is now unlocked for everyone. After watching all of it (I'm not playing that cause I hate hallucinatory/acid trip stuff in videogame campaigns for personal reasons), I'd rate the campaign a [b]2.5/10[/b]. Please don't try the RE shtick, you suck at it, Raven.

The golden part of this game, however, is the [b]Multiplayer.[/b] First of all, [b]it is the ONLY Multiplayer made in the last 6 years that does not have FULL ON MW2019 SBMM BY DEFAULT[/b]. Some people are complaining it's still there, however, the devs DID say there IS some SBMM, not ZERO, so I chalk that up as either a skill issue, or someone being such an omega tryhard that they still get put through the ringer. And uh, that's no one's fault but yours, bud, maybe don't spam the Meta™ weapon, tactics, and equipment every game to beat up 40 year old construction worker fathers who just got off a 10 hour shift in the blistering heat and want to relax? Just a hunch, tho.

Anyways, just this change has made BO7's multiplayer one of the top MPs of the last 6 years for me, not counting Cold War, which I felt was the best one (excluding BOCW's bad scorestreak system, that is). [b]It also has no tactical sprint by default[/b] and the scorestreaks are actually kinda great (aside from a few that need buffs like the Hellstorm). It is very fun and fast-paced, but right now there's a LOT of sweats cause the casuals got scared away from this game by the (somewhat justified, but also grifted to high hell) hate it received for the mediocre campaign. The maps are ALL good (aside from IMO, Flagship, which is a small map that takes place at a shipyard under a ship being built, but that's probably me getting my ass beat on that map every time), which is not usual for CoD lately. Hell, they even brought back Hijacked and Raid from BO2, and Standoff and Meltdown will be coming back as Season 1 maps (with three other original maps) in Dec 4th! The items you have access to are also quite creative. The Psych Grenade/Fear Trap essentially putting people under a Genjutsu that spawns fake clones everywhere and changes everyone's model to the victim's own while also taking away the ability to discern friend AND hallucinations from foes is extremely funny to observe, especially when the dude affected by it starts shooting literal air 😂 I'd give the MP a solid [b]8.5/10.[/b]

The Zombies mode is also considered okay or even decent by people who aren't grifting hate views out of it, I just haven't played it yet, but I do plan to do so in the future. I do like the return of the OG crew, I just wish Ritchtofen wasn't a, uh, you-know-what again. I'll probably edit my review once I play it, tho.

I would give this game a solid 7/10, overall. [b]If you enjoy the Call of Duty gameplay loop in Multiplayer, and likes fast-paced arcade shooters, there shouldn't be a reason for you to not play this game[/b]. Just uh, [i]avoid the campaign like the plague.[/]

I'll list it under Recommended cause I genuinely like this game's MP AND the Zombies mode seems good, but again: Do not bother with the campaign, it's beyond awful. Just load straight into Multiplayer, or, if you want to know the story, read it on the CoD Wiki or in Wikipedia itself. Or watch it on Youtube if you're brave enough.

Oh, and [b]if you choose Kagan as your Guild operator you are exposing to everyone the fact you like evil goth chicks and probably went ballistic with the Blackfire dance scene on the original Teen Titans show.[/b] I know what you are, kid.

[h3] General Info [/h3]
[b] Before I start I'm just going to say I'm NOT going to glaze the game nor am I going to paint it in a pessimistic way that recent trends have been doing. [/b] Very likely going to go down as the most overhated Call of Duty of all time. Not even close to a "dlc" as some people are stating. Never in the history of games has a dlc had as much new content as Black Ops 7 currently has off launch. The game has a significant amount of QoL features and new additions (overclocks, wall hops, hybrid perks, cursed mode, survival maps are back for the 3rd time ever, minimal sbmm, an entire extraction mode with it's own mastery camos, new scorestreaks, 25% rotational aim assist nerf, etc.) 

They cancelled several big franchise crossovers and the season 1 skins including blackcell are very minimal and on theme for the games style which was a massive complaint of the last game. They also slowed down the movement from BO6 which most people complained about too. Both Black Ops 4 and Black Ops 3 which people tend to look fondly at, for one reason or another both had no campaign or an equally bad campaign, but it was overlooked due to all their other modes being fun, so I don't see what changed so much since then that everyone feels the need to rate a game based on 1 of literally 6 gamemodes (Multiplayer, Zombies, Dead Ops, Extraction, Campaign, Warzone).

[h3] Zombies [/h3]
As someone who's been playing Zombies since WaW I just have to say I enjoyed most of the gameplay changes BO6 Zombies made excluding several features like no wall planks, weapon loadouts, over crowded UI, the whole map being flooded in 2 seconds with zombies and armor using warzone plates instead of having a zombie mode tailored model. As far as armor goes it's probably one of the more over hated mechanics considering the old Zombie Riot Shields were literally just ripped straight from multiplayer/campaign but with a skin and ability slapped on but that doesn't excuse the new plates not even having that skin/ability old zombie shields would have per map.

Most people negative or positive seem to agree the zombies so far is extremely good. The level of sci-fi is back to what Black Ops 3 had which was the fan favorite for zombies. Ashes of the Damned has an incredibly fun layout and visual design with lots of old location themes but remade to feel entirely new but visually familiar. Tessie, the driveable and upgradeable truck feels much better than the boat from Terminus did and is on par with the old Tranzit bus as far as fun goes. The boss was fun, unique to play against and nailed that grotesque visual look that the Terminus boss had. There are brand new Elite/Special zombies for every map again instead of re-using the same ones for all of them like BO6 did. Black Ops 7 introduces Cursed mode which brings back several of the old mechanics including the old point system, no armor, starting pistol and significantly limited/classic style hud along with some optional difficulty challenges.

Dead Ops arcade 4 is here and as someone who always loved the mode in Black Ops 1 back in the day I can assure anyone who wants to try this mode out that it's as fun as it always was. There's a couple new additions like gobblegum which have custom abilities just for this mode, new powerups, new minigames, and more. 

[h3] Multiplayer [/h3]
We are 24 games into Call of Duty so I feel I can easily say that the wall hops are a fun and unique movement addition and are so much better than having a 20th game with boots on the ground movement while not being nearly as overkill as Exo Jumps or Thrust Jumps. There are 15 new and 3 remastered maps. Not even close to as much re-used content as people are stating. Most of them have good layouts for the 3 lane style. The new overclocks are a small but good addition and the hybrid perks fill the gap that Black Ops 6 had that forced you to use 3 same color perks for the bonus. It's been so long since CoD has had that classic SBMM it's hard to tell how good the new minimal SBMM is but from my experience the lobbies tend to have a couple good and a couple bad players on both sides almost every time, take that how you will.

[h3] The Ugly [/h3]
We've seen our fair share of weird/bad campaign moments in CoD games before but this one just feels different. Nearly every single moment from start to finish feels as tacky as they could have possibly made it to be. It feels scummy locking a full extraction mode which I know a chunk of the playerbase liked in MW2 (DMZ) and MW3 (MWZ) behind the mode that everyone, negative or positive view point on the game agrees is complete sh**. 

The AI calling cards is the lowest effort possible and completely unnecessary making it hard to be overlooked despite how tiny of a part of the game it is. I would sincerely hope they take notice of everyone hating them for this and change it like they did so many other features that were complained about. Will this hurt your actual enjoyment of the game though? probably not.

If I could I would put this game a side thumb rating because I do not recommend it nor am I stating you shouldn't get it. If you like Call of Duty, this game is just more of that though unarguably starting stronger than MW2, MW3, or BO6 did. They absolutely should move on from Modern Warfare and Black Ops and start a new game series with it's own engine variant keeping all the QoL changes they went through with this game.

Black Ops 7 is great in certain areas and abysmal in others.

Let's start with the negative, campaign. To start, the campaign is certainly not a classic Call of Duty experience and ultimately a disappointment. It feels like it belongs in an entirely different Sci-Fi universe rather than in the Call of Duty world, and even at that fails to be well done. You cannot pause the campaign and ultimately it just feels like a failed project on that front. The campaign is a complete and utter failure.

Now lets move on to the first positive, multiplayer. While people who are low skill will not enjoy it, this Call of Duty listens to the competitive player that has been forgotten about since 2019. With reduced skill based matchmaking I am finally able to play the game with my lower skilled friends and everyone is enjoying it rather than no one in complete sweat lobbies. On top of that, there was a much needed aim assist nerf and now you actually have to aim for yourself. The maps have been a big step up from recent titles and flow much better as well. My only complaint at launch is weapon balancing which can be corrected with future updates.

Last, my favorite part of this game is something I think has been vastly underrated since original launch, Dead Ops Arcade. I have loved this series since it first released, and they did it even better with this years title. It's not just an arcade like shooter, but there are mini games where you can race in time trials, fly a chopper, play an arcade like shooter mid round and overall I think they did a fantastic job upgrading this series in this game. 

Overall, I'm a fan of this game, but I don't buy it for campaign I buy it for multiplayer and zombies. If those are the things you're looking for, and you give the game a legitimate chance, I think you will come to enjoy it.

I'm not a COD hater but this has to be the worst game they've ever released. I'll breakdown each game mode and why it's so bad.

Campaign - No real set pieces, terrible writing, confusing plot, multiple plot holes and zero replay value. The Bosses here are extremely spongey and offer very little satisfaction or challenge. This whole campaign feels rushed and unfinished. Not to mention a lot of the moments shown in the previews for this game don't appear in the final campaign. Most of the marketed moments don't actually happen in the campaign.

Multiplayer - They gutted everything good about Black Ops 6 MP and it's movement. The game now feels extremely clunky with various design decisions fighting each other. They want you to bounce off the walls while also moving like a snail on the ground.

Zombies - Removal of LTMs and modes like Grief. Ashes is definitely better than Terminus but Vandorn Farm doesn't fill the gap left by Liberty Falls. Like the rest of the game it feels shallow and doesn't entice me to play it more, if anything it's the opposite. 

Endgame - Reskinned MWZ with essentially no progression. They reskinned zombies perks into skill trees and killstreaks into minor abilities. The whole mode is essentially driven by camo grinding and unlocking operators.

Pre-Order - Advertised skins and bonuses were cut after the game was already for sale. Essentially this means players pre-ordered the game under the guise that certain content would be made available to them which Treyarch then cancelled without proper notice. This goes beyond COD and could set a dangerous precedent for pre-order bonuses moving forward. 

Carry Forward - This was also advertised as a feature and was only changed after pre-orders went live. The biggest problem I have with this is that they cancelled it only to selectively carry forward specific pieces of content and ultimately costing the players 2/3 of the weapon arsenal. [h3]Campaign[/h3]

Giving reasons on why there are certain people coming back, building upon the "cradle" from BO6's storyline and giving general ways that the regular call of duty campaign universe connects to the zombies universe all connecting and making sense in their respective timelines. Then the "Endgame" gamemode which is unlocked at the end turns the campaign into a fully fledged open world that further builds upon the story. Despite what people say, I would rate this campaign a [u]7/10[/u] would be an [u]8/10[/u] but honestly the endgame gamemode just doesn't fill the void of the short campaign.

The endmode gamemode is a pretty fun extraction shooter with similar mechanics to warzone. It adds a skill system that upgrades as you collect the cradle's essence from killing NPCs. while being online so you are with quite a few other players on this very large Verdansk sized map. This gamemode is NOT just a warzone gamemode clone, it has its own qualities and is quite chill. It has qualities from MW3s open world zombies, including zones that have harder difficulty that you can only make it too by selecting your skills correctly and getting lucky to roll for the right skills after achieving a certain number of kills. 


[h3]Zombies[/h3]

Like previous CoD games, the zombies storyline continues with Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. As of writing this review there is only one main map with an Easter Egg. The easter egg has many, many steps and is very challenging to complete. I would equate the boss fight to BO6s zombies "Terminus" while having the complexity of the "Citadelle Des Morts" Easter egg in BO6. The map brings back a mechanic well known in BO2, TranZit! Now cool it, it's not the TranZit you are thinking of. It innovates on the idea and changes many aspects, but it is very similar to TranZit from BO2. ★★★★☆ — Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 Review

After putting over 40 hours into Black Ops 7, I feel confident in saying this is one of the most fun entries in the franchise in years — even if it’s not flawless.

My personal highlight is still Zombies. Treyarch absolutely nailed it again. The maps are layered without being confusing, the pacing ramps up perfectly, and the loop of upgrading, surviving, and experimenting with new builds is ridiculously addictive. It’s hands-down the mode I’ve spent most of my time in.

Multiplayer is consistently strong as well. The gunplay feels crisp, the maps have a good mix of ranges and sightlines, and the meta hasn’t fallen apart — yet. It’s that classic “one more match” formula that Black Ops has always done well.

Where the game struggles is the campaign. It isn’t terrible — there are missions that genuinely shine — but overall it’s sloppy. The pacing jumps around, character arcs feel undercooked, and the story tries to juggle more than it can hold. Still, it’s a fun enough ride, and I pushed through it mostly to reach the post-campaign endgame, where the real grind begins.

The endgame content that unlocks after beating the campaign is where Black Ops 7 really opens up. Progression systems deepen, difficulty ramps in a meaningful way, and there’s a rewarding chase for weapons, cosmetics, and stat-based advancement. It gives the game long-term legs beyond the standard multiplayer loop.

⸻

Final Verdict

Black Ops 7 has some rough edges — mainly the campaign — but it absolutely delivers where it counts: addictive Zombies, solid multiplayer, and a surprisingly robust post-campaign endgame that keeps the grind exciting.

I’ve stuck with this series longer than I should’ve, and this is the first time I’m sitting here like, “Yeah… maybe it’s time to let it die.” The campaign alone is enough to make you question what the hell they’re doing. Calling this a sequel to BO2 is just insane. BO2 had one of the strongest stories in COD, and this new campaign basically spits on it. Nothing feels serious, nothing feels grounded — it’s boss fights, random scorestreaks, giant machetes from the sky, and writing that feels like it was slapped together last minute by ChatGPT. It doesn’t feel like Black Ops at all.

Then multiplayer hits and somehow it’s not much better. It’s not completely unplayable, but it’s just… nothing. It’s bland. It’s forgettable. 

And zombies? Same story. It’s not terrible, but it’s completely watered down. It doesn’t feel scary, it doesn’t feel tense, and it doesn’t feel like zombies. It’s just another mode you play for a bit and then forget about. They keep drifting further away from what made zombies special in the first place, and now it feels like a side activity instead of a big deal.

That’s what hurts the most: the series has no direction anymore. Every part of this game feels like it was made by a team that doesn’t know what COD is supposed to be. The campaign ruins the past, multiplayer is a snooze, and zombies is just there because it has to be. If they keep going like this, COD isn’t just going downhill — it’s going to end up completely forgettable.

I’m not even mad because I hate the series. I’m mad because I defended it for years, and this is what we got in return.

During the lead up to Black Ops 7's release, Call of Duty made a big deal about the discontinuation of carry forward, the cancellation of collaborative cosmetics, and removal of SBMM from casual playlists. Turns out that this was nothing but a smokescreen to get people's feet in the door of what may be the laziest video game ever produced.

Black Ops 7's multiplayer barely innovates on its predecessor. While Omni-movement remains an under-utilized gimmick, the addition of wall jumping does add a useful tool for navigating combat. Unfortunately, the multiplayer maps are scared to properly utilize the mechanic to its fullest potential like we saw with wall-running in Black Ops 3, and some maps don't have any real use for it at all. Most egregious among these are the reprisals from Black Ops 2, which dominate the map vote but have not been adapted to the new gameplay mechanics, rendering them all but useless. Add to that the new maps being mediocre at best and abysmal at worst, creating another entry of mediocre multiplayer modes unwilling to innovate their design.

I have not played the Zombies mode in my 9 hours of playtime, but considering that I have been playing Call of Duty since 2010, and enjoyed Zombies a whole lot over these past 15 years, the fact that the return of the original Zombies cast failed to drum up any real interest in playing the mode in the slightest does not fill me with confidence. Plus, they decided to make a spiritual successor to TranZit, and I do not recall that map being particularly well-loved.

And, of course, the campaign. You have undoubtedly heard things about Black Ops 7's campaign. Whatever you think you know, I assure you it is 10 times worse. The plot is incoherent, and the game's villain is all but non-existent. Not for lack of a villain, mind you, as the game immediately reveals its big plot twist 5 minutes in, but because they play almost zero role in the plot and their evil plan is laughably predictable. The boss fights are all terrible, and all the missions have at least one. Half the time it is some sort of Guild hardware, either a turret or a VTOL or a robot, and the other half its some random Multiplayer operator that teleports whenever you shoot them. Both are terrible. Giant Harper is also terrible, but you've seen Giant Harper. Hilariously enough, the best boss fight is the one that I can only assume was made by someone who really likes fighting the Pyro Regisvine from Genshin Impact, but even that is horrendously bad. The game has 11 missions, with every other mission being walking around the presumably upcoming Warzone map for 20 minutes, a mode whose mechanics are also littered throughout the campaign. The other half the missions are all reused assets, mostly multiplayer maps, and including one egregious example where the game reuses a portion of one of Black Ops 6's campaign missions in Vorkuta. The main cast can barely be considered characters. David Mason continues his previous role of "Standard White Man in a CoD game", Harper has been reduced to rage and one-liners, 50/50 has some vaguely tragic backstory about a massacre in Japan which she was present for for some reason, and Samuels is there. Ironically, the best mission in the game is the one where you play as JSOC's multiplayer operators, who actually have personalities. The Endgame mode is not worth playing the campaign to unlock, and this is coming from someone who played a whole lot of MWII's DMZ. 

Two final things:
1. This game has an odd obsession with Japan, to the point that it was seemingly the focal point of the game's marketing. This means half the multiplayer maps are inexplicably set in Japan. It's especially odd since they said that this would be the "first Black Ops with maps set in Japan", despite BO2's Magma and BO4's Gridlock being set in Japan.
2. The very big issue: Activision has riddled this game with AI-generated assets. Calling Cards, Prestige icons, and I would not be shocked if it's eventual storefront used AI art as well. There is even speculation that AI was used to write the campaign, but these are unfounded and I'm not sure that I believe it, regardless of how bad it was. Either way, Activision has made it abundantly clear that this was a conscious choice and seemingly has no intentions of changing course.

In a year in which DICE and EA did everything in its power to revitalize the public perception of the Battlefield franchise, Call of Duty has decided to cement itself as a pillar to corporate greed and a giant middle finger to the concept of video games as creative works. Activision has actively decided that the most profitable video game franchise in history would be reduced to nothing but slop in favor of making as much money as possible as it reuses assets, plot points, and characters from previous games and screw over its artists as it generates its most intricate 2D assets the series has had for over 15 years. My only hope is that someone at Activision realizes the blight they have created in this medium and the company does a massive course correction in the coming years, but I know that this is a monster created by myself and the millions of others that have bought increasingly lazy CoD games over the past few years. The one good thing to come out of this game is that it has finally succeeded in breaking me free of the Stockholm Syndrome this series has locked me in for the past decade.

Hence, all my playtime is on the Call of Duty app, since you can't have playtime on Black Ops 7 specifically since its not an application.

Review: Call of Duty: Black Ops 7
Score: 7/10
TL;DR: BO7 delivers fast, satisfying multiplayer and finally adds a co-op campaign—something fans have wanted for years. But mandatory co-op, supernatural chaos, and the franchise’s increasingly formulaic identity keep it from greatness.
________________________________________
A Promising Idea With Uneven Execution
Let’s get the basics out of the way: Black Ops 7 actually runs quite well for me. No crashes, no sound bugs, no “my gun disappeared mid-cutscene” moments. Voice acting? Solid. Visuals? Polished. For once, a AAA shooter shipped mostly finished (at least for my experience). Already a miracle in 2025.
And yes—the co-op campaign is finally here. Years of players shouting “LET ME PLAY COD WITH MY FRIENDS” seemingly paid off. Unfortunately, whoever designed the system also decided that the campaign must be online and must assume you have four friends at all times. If you play solo or with one buddy, half your squad simply evaporates between cutscenes and gameplay as if Thanos snapped them out of existence. It’s not game-breaking, but it’s definitely sloppy.
The campaign itself leans hard into the supernatural. It isn’t the grounded military thriller on which the series built its name. Think Gears of War energy but with more neon. The upside? The boss fights. They’re big, creative, and a bit chaotic—in the best way. You’ll fight enemies that look like they wandered in from a completely different franchise, and honestly, it works. It’s fun, even if “realism” packed its bags, left the country, and never sent a postcard.
Just accept the nonsense, enjoy the ride, and you’ll have a good time.
________________________________________
Multiplayer: Familiar, Fast, and Comfortably Chaotic
Multiplayer is classic Call of Duty: fast, snappy, instantly familiar. Treyarch hasn’t reinvented anything here, nor have they dramatically improved much—did anyone actually expect them to? If you’ve played a COD in the last decade, you’ve essentially played this one.
That said, it’s still fun. Very fun!
The futuristic setting is convincing, from flashy 2050s-style weapon designs to EMP grenades that fry cybernetically enhanced enemies. Movement and physics feel subtly refined—snappier, more responsive. Landing a quick headshot has that perfect “click”—the kind of moment where you instinctively mutter, “Bro, that kid is so mad right now.”
In terms of identity, though, BO7 is in a strange place. It’s not as “realistic” as Battlefield 6, and it’s not as playful or over-the-top as something like Marvel Rivals. It’s inching toward a Titanfall-lite experience but doesn’t fully commit. The result is fun but directionless—good enough that I won’t go back to Black Ops 6, but far from groundbreaking.
________________________________________
The Annual Formula Problem
And this is where Call of Duty starts to resemble the WWE 2K series: a formulaic, annualized product that rarely evolves in meaningful ways. Year after year, a new skin, a handful of new mechanics, a batch of maps, and then—boom—onto the next release. At least with something like Madden, we get a meaningful roster update.
It raises an uncomfortable question: Does Call of Duty actually benefit from being yearly anymore? Probably not.
A multi-year development cycle could give this franchise the space it desperately needs to rediscover a cohesive identity—because right now, it feels like the devs are duct-taping ideas together: a little Titanfall here, a little supernatural chaos there, some nostalgic maps sprinkled on top, and voilà—another $70 installment.
Black Ops 7 is a good game. But it could’ve been a great one.
________________________________________
Should You Buy It?
Buy BO7 if:
1.	You always buy the new COD and want fresh maps, zombies, and progression.
2.	You prefer COD’s chaotic-but-slick FPS feel over Battlefield 6’s dusty walking/tank simulator.
3.	You want a co-op campaign, even if it’s unhinged and structurally weird.
If none of those apply, you’re safe waiting—or skipping entirely.

Okay there's a LOT to cover with this game surprisingly. I'll try to be as non-biased as possible. I AM a long time CoD fan, but I can still acknowledge that this game has strayed very far from it's identity.

The Good:

- The movement feels really nice, I'm a huge fan of the new wall jump as it opens up a lot of outplay opportunities as well as opening up new routing options around the map.

- The gunplay feels really, really good. I play on M&K, as its always felt more natural to me than playing controller. For a while I had my gripes with aim assist, and it feels like I have more of a fighting chance against controller players in close range fights now which is great. If I do lose a gunfight to a controller player, I can atleast feel like it was earned and not due to RAA being absurdly overtuned. 

- Visibility is LEAGUES better than in previous titles. While it's still not great, I feel like I can actually see enemies around the map now instead of them blending in or losing sight through smoke effects/explosions. The health bar helps a lot with this, and I'm a big fan of this being brought back.

- New maps are GREAT. I'm pressed to say this is the best set of new, original maps in a Call of Duty title in a long time. There are maybe one or two maps I'm not a big fan of, but the rest are all really strong and flow really well.

The Bad:

- The campaign. This campaign is a MASSIVE disappointment. I wouldn't even call it a step down in quality, it is genuinely an outright embarrassment and a smear on the Black Ops name AND the Call of Duty IP as a whole. It feels like Treyarch hired a 16 year old to write this story, it's incredibly tone-deaf, inconsistent, and I genuinely believe it undermines the legacy the BO2 campaign built. On top of all of that, it leans into that Warzone-style mission design that MWIII used, which I feel confident in saying NO ONE enjoyed.

- Zombies. While I don't think zombies is nearly as bad as the disaster that is the campaign, I do think it feels a little half baked at the moment. I will also say I haven't played very much zombies, so I don't think I can comment a lot on it. I have heard about the cursed mode essentially being like BO3 zombies, which sounds fun and is something I'd be interested in trying.

- Multiplayer maps being remastered for the 60th time. While a lot of the new, original maps are very strong and feel nice, I am getting a little sick of seeing the same remastered maps over and over again. Don't get me wrong, it is nice to get to come back to some of these remastered maps - especially Raid - but this is the 4th time we've seen Hijacked and Raid if you include the BO3 remakes. I would've really liked to see some other BO2 maps get the spotlight if we're just reusing old maps, such as Carrier, Plaza, or Meltdown. 

- Spawns are a bit chaotic in TDM at the moment, and I feel like they flip a little too often, leaving some maps to feel like you're hunting for engagements more than you're actually in them. I feel like this will be tuned as the game ages so it's not a big negative for me.

- The minimap in MP almost feels useless, even if you run Vigilance. It's way too zoomed in, and I feel like you're better off using your compass to search for fights than using the minimap.

The Ugly:

- AI. This is the largest complaint I see and I fully understand it as there is zero excuse for a company this large to be using AI-generated cosmetics and assets. The AI calling cards look like your average Studio Ghibli filter AI slop and I genuinely wish this wasn't the case. I know they will not stop using these assets, so at the bare MINIMUM it would be nice if they weren't so blatantly AI generated and they at least attempted to hide it.

- Always online. While this has been a pretty common occurrence with recent CoD titles, it's still a pretty big turn off for me. I'd love to play Zombies offline if the servers are down or I lose internet. This applies to EVERYTHING, so even if you wanted to play this horrendous campaign for some reason, you can't.

- Cosmetics. We all know it will inevitably happen down the road. The shop will be filled with a ton of slop, and there's a pretty good chance a lot of it will be AI generated or assisted.

Overall, Black Ops 7 is a mixed bag in my opinion. The core gameplay is pretty strong. The new, original maps feel amazing. The campaign is absolute horseshit and I feel like anyone could write a better plotline, and the AI generated assets and cosmetics are a huge turn off for a lot of people, myself included.

If you buy CoD for the multiplayer, like I do, I can recommend it; just not at full price. I would wait for a sale.

Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 isn’t a campaign it’s an 80€ advertisement for Warzone, and in my case a 110€ personal tragedy thanks to the Vault Edition.
At this point, I’m convinced the Vault Edition includes: 1 skin, 1 blueprint, and a certificate of regret for your wallet.

Finishing this “campaign” made me rethink my life choices. All of them. Maybe even past lives too.

Story Mode

At first, I thought damn coop campaign, this might be good. 
But calling this a story is like calling a puddle the Pacific Ocean, you can't play alone, you can't go AFK cause you'll get kicked OUT in a campaign yes, you can't pause because it's always online so you can't pause.
No focus, no emotional weight, no purpose, the map Avalon it's an open map like warzone where you roam around and kill enemies with no logical reason.
The MW3 reboot campaign which the entire fanbase trashed suddenly looks like Oscar winning cinema in comparison.
The entire campaign is stuffed with: recycled BO6 zombie models, mutated monsters, giant bosses, weird insect like creatures (still recycled from BO6), and other assets dragged from the BO6 trash bin.
A Black Ops game turned into a sci fi monster shooter?
Who asked for this?
Nobody. Literally nobody.

Gameplay

The gameplay is a catastrophe built on copy paste level design and rushed production.
The next CoD was announced in under a year, so what did we expect?
Effort? Quality? Innovation?
Hahahaha. No.
Everything feels rushed, shallow, and uninspired.
Boss fights look like rejected ideas from Destiny 2.
Missions are lifeless corridors.
Gunplay is flat.
Stealth doesn’t exist.
Tension doesn’t exist.
Meaning doesn’t exist.

Multiplayer

It’s literally BO6 with a few tweaks, a couple of rearranged maps, and a fresh coat of marketing paint.
Sometimes it can be satisfying very occasionally but for the most part it just feels like you’re paying again for something you already played last year. 
If BO6 multiplayer bored you, BO7 won’t save you.

Zombie Mode

I haven’t tried Zombies yet.
But considering everything else I’ve seen?
I’m expecting nothing more than a copy paste BO6 zombie mode, maybe even worse, depending on how much content they had time to recycle this time. I’ll be shocked if it turns out to be anything but reused mechanics, reused maps, reused enemies, and reused ideas, but to be honest I don't even have the grit to play this mode since I got traumatized already with the campaign.

Sound & Dialogue

Characters sound like they're reading off cue cards in a bathroom.
Dialogue feels AI generated.
Atmosphere is non existent.
Effects are hollow.
It’s a void an expensive void.

Achievements

I still didn't finish all the Achievements and I don't think I will, I'll try "maybe", but they probably are so easy it almost feels intentional.
The game wants you to finish fast, uninstall, and go touch grass for emotional recovery.

Conclusion

Black Ops 7 is: rushed, shallow, directionless, stuffed with recycled assets, full of monster enemies nobody asked for, written without the minimal effort, and sold at 80€, or 110€ if you made my mistake.
The worst part?
The whole “campaign” is nothing more than a glorified Warzone commercial.
I’ve made many mistakes in life…
but buying the 110€ Vault Edition of this might be the final boss of regret.
Final Note – If You Want a Real Shooter, Play Something Else
If you want a shooter that actually represents real warfare, with a proper military tone and a real campaign,
just go play Battlefield 6.
The campaign is actually a military story, and missions feel grounded, and you won’t be fighting zombies, insects, or giant fantasy bosses that look like they escaped from BO6’s zombie recycle bin.

The multiplayer is absolutely the best it's been in a long time. 

The maps actually feel like they're designed and have loads of interesting different pathways as well as interesting interactables and cool hard to reach areas through wall jumping. Each map also actually has a lot of color, and the colors of each map are distinct and the locations and buildings etc. are too, they don't all just feel like generic parts of a city or military base. The maps also utilize the futuristic setting, making for some really neat set pieces. I'm looking forward to some maps that utilize the hallucinogenic gas to make them really crazy.

Beyond the map designs, the guns also feel really good and some of them have neat futuristic twists to them, like the charge shotgun and energy rpg. The tacticals and lethals are also really interesting and varied this time around too. Having new perk specialists for mixed perk types is also really cool!

Also you can actually gib people and shoot their limbs off again, players don't just ragdoll anymore. 

Also they got rid of skill-based match making which I personally never thought was actually a problem, but now seeing how much more fun I'm having it's clear it was a problem and I hope they never bring it back.

Aside from the multiplayer, the zombies is also really promising.

The new Ashes of Damned map is really unique and interesting and has a bunch of unique mechanics like the truck and jump pads to interact with, interesting special zombies, things that make the map feel different and special unlike a lot of the BO6 maps. Also the new cursed mode is great and really does make it feel a lot closer to older zombies. I hope the next maps are just as good and hopefully even better.

Lastly the campaign, though I haven't played much of it, seems fine.

The campaign doesn't seem like much more than a fun multiplayer PvE mode like zombies, but if the zombies had guns. It having replayable endgame content sounds pretty interesting though. The only complaints I've seen is that it isn't realistic, but like it's a video game, set in the future, with hallucinatory gas, why not use that to make the game more fun and crazy? If you want a more grounded experience play one of the 50,000 other realistic war shooters.

An actually valid complaint is that at least half if not more of the calling cards in the base game are AI generated which is awful. A couple of the calling cards in BO6 were AI generated, but I was hoping they'd stop doing that here. Sadly they went even harder on it making almost all of the calling cards feel like soulless garbage. It's such a shame because I love the calling card systems in Treyarch games, collecting all of the neat HUMAN made pieces of art in all sorts of different styles kind of like Pokemon cards, but now it's completely ruined. It would literally cost so little to pay artists to make some calling cards compared to how much profit they make. I worry that soon they'll be replacing much more than just the calling cards with AI.

I am still recommending this game because the gameplay is great, especially the multiplayer, but just barely. The AI calling cards are shameful and I hope they replace them.

I’ve put about 12 hours into Zombies only, and honestly: it’s a good time, but not my Zombies anymore.

Gameplay-wise, the movement feels great and ripping through big hordes with numbers popping off is satisfying. Abilities like Dark Aether Beam and Aether Shroud help keep things engaging, and the camo grind is actually faster than Cold War. Rank XP feels fine too.

But almost everything else lacks personality. The guns all look, sound, and feel the same – I can’t remember a single weapon name. Camos look like AI art, maps feel a bit soulless and don’t show off any real graphical fidelity, and scrap economy makes most bullet guns useless by round 40 unless you’re perfectly upgraded.

On PC, it’s rough technically. It runs fine at first, then the moment you pause, FPS randomly drops to ~50–55 and the game starts chugging until you restart. The timed pause menu is annoying, and rejoining after being kicked from pause feels laggy as hell. I’ve had constant netcode warnings and one crash. Compared to Cold War, this looks worse, runs worse, and feels far less stable.

Progression is spammy too – constant popups trying to manufacture dopamine. It feels more aimed at kids now than classic Zombies grinders.

Who I’d recommend it to:

Zombies players desperate for new content and willing to eat launch jank.

Who I wouldn’t:

Anyone wanting a classic-feeling Zombies experience or a stable game right now. BO3 modded is still the better recommendation.

This might genuinely be one of the worst Call of Duty releases to date. The entire game feels like AI-generated slop: lifeless, dull, and completely stripped of any personality or soul. The maps are boring and repetitive, the SBMM claims were blatant lies, and the matchmaking is suffocatingly heavy every single match.

The few returning classic maps are the only positive thing here, but even they feel cheap and hollow. This entire release comes across like a low-effort DLC for BO6, not a full-priced game.

And speaking of price — charging 80€ for this is insane. Every year, the series gets worse, and this time they didn’t even pretend to care. Campaign and Zombies aren’t worth mentioning: the campaign is one of the weakest in the franchise’s history, and the Zombies mode feels empty and rushed. Even the camos look cheap.

Overall, this game is a 3/10 at best. The franchise has officially lost its spark, talent, and creativity. For me, this is the moment Call of Duty finally dies. A greedy, soulless release from a company that no longer cares about its players.

This is a difficult game. On one hand, it has many of the good staples of a classic CoD game. On the other; it is deluded with AI and seems to be catering to a Fortnite audience as well as missing a number of important parts of what makes Call of Duty good. 

Pros: 
- SBMM is toned down significantly, making the multiplayer a lot more enjoyable in the process. Same goes for consistent lobbies. This however, is the bare minimum. The player base has been screaming for these changes since MW19 and they suddenly listen when Battlefield 6 dominates the FPS-market, coincidence, huh? 
- Zombies is fun although not as fleshed out as BO6, definitely better than CW or Vanguard, but not anywhere near the classic zombies experiences including BO4, BO3, BO2, WaW or even BO6.

Cons: 
- Co-op campaign much like MW3. Abysmal. Truly a cash-crab set in warzone-assets they hadn't yet found the time to use. Calling this a campaign is very generous. 
- Skins are definitely not going to remain 'grounded' for long. The game screams 'egregious microtransactions incoming', I guess we'll have to wait and see for season 1. 
- Massive packet-burst issues on PC, no matter your connection type. Major issue I hope gets worked out soon. 

All in all, this feels like BO6.5 without the price tag reflecting it. Multiplayer may be fun and zombies as well, but an awful campaign and stuck in the context of other great multiplayer games currently available such as BF6 and Arc Raiders (some for free; see Marvel Rivals) this Call of Duty honestly doesn't seem to cater to very many people. 

Do I recommend it? It's okay, but if you want to spend your hard-earned money on a great multiplayer experience - then buy Arc Raiders or Battlefield 6. I'd give this game a 6/10.

Played only MP for now (yeah, skipped beta because BF6 hype had me in a chokehold) and played a bit of campaign. So here are my thoughts.

[h2]Call of Duty BO7 is… Call of Duty as it is. Let’s be frank guys: when you go to buy “Snickers,” you get a Snickers. No one is hoping to unwrap a 3-piece meal from that chocolate bar. Same logic here — you love CoD? Congrats, this is 100% CoD with all its pros and cons, side effects, and recommended doses.[/h2]

PROS:
• No BO6 skins — huge win. My eyes finally get a break from Family Guy, clowns, Beavis, anime catgirls, and whatever fever-dream bundles BO6 dropped on us. Hopefully BO7 stays clean until Season 1… or at least until Activision remembers they love money.
• No SBMM — finally I can stay in the same lobby like in the good old days before matchmaking tried to ruin my self-esteem.
• Fast TTK — FINALLY in a BO game. And after 70+ hours of BF6, the feeling of guns actually killing instead of politely asking enemies to fall is amazing. (And BF players with 1.5+ K\D — please explain how you did that without shotguns, KORD 6P67, or NVO-228E. I’ll wait.)
• Good progression system — just like BO6: start at level 1, unlock all guns, prestige yourself, prestige your guns… feels like old-school CoD grind that actually works.

CONS:
• The price. In my country that starts with U and ends with kraine, BO7 costs about 2× BF6. I guess I’m officially the only insane person here who bought BOTH. I’m begging devs to let us buy modes separately someday. What if I just want to grind MP until I become a grandpa? Why do I have to pay for Zombies and Campaign I’ll never touch again?
• Optimization — overall okay, but packet loss happens way too often. Maybe it’s my internet, maybe refresh rate, maybe cosmic punishment. But in the fastest CoD since BO3 every tiny issue is vital.
• Not much OG weapons yet. Really hope AN-94, Skorpion EVO, PRK, Galil etc show up in the battle pass… but that also means I’ll have to grind all seasons like it’s a second job. Not excited for that.

OVERALL:
Honestly, I expected worse. The main problem with CoD isn’t the devs — they’re doing fine. It’s the managers who refused to listen until BF6 slapped them with a “this is what the audience actually wants” example. So yeah, some small but important changes already make BO7 feel a bit like OG CoD again. And overall it feels closer to BO3 than BO6, at least to me.

Totals:
[h2]CoD fans: yeah, you’ll enjoy it.
BF6 enjoyers: you’ll find nothing here (movement-based, no 100-meter shotgun one-shots, no K/D farming on bots… and maps are surprisingly not cramped for CoD standards. Which is honestly a surprise. Yeah - BF6's Saints Quarter will hardly be surpassed by any of the current BO7 maps (and hopefully the future ones too).
Is it BO6 DLC? Nah. Feels more like BO3’s younger cousin.
Will CoD fans buy it anyway? Yes.
Does this review matter? Probably not.[/h2]

No... just no... this game was the literal definition of screwing... no... f***ing the pooch.  The campaign alone was absolute trash, some elements were nice, somewhat open world to explore a little further than a normal campaign map.  Utilization of minor abilities like a grapple hook, and whatever major ability you chose for your play style.  Lot of potential in other areas.  But story was beyond flaming garbage.  I liked that Harper looks like the voice actor Michael Rooker, even though it threw me off seeing he didn't look like OG Harper.  Yet they chose to have him as a "trippy" kaiju boss fight?  Why, just why?  Speaking of which why is everything centered around being in a hallucination every single f***ing mission?  The trailer alone made me think there was some serious shit going on. Especially with Mason being in civie's.  That usually equates into some undercover work, like when they infiltrated the skyscraper in BO2 to get Karma.  Also the dialogue was pretty f***ing painful.  Like sandpaper on the skin, followed by rubbing alcohol and salt.  Some moments were nice, but too rare and far between.  And back to the hallucination stuff, why did Woods become much more weaker than his previous iterations?  If we really wanted to get into the trauma of him in Vietnam they could've done better story telling, like the flashback missions in BO2 or better yet the entirety of what was BO1.  And I didn't even play BO1.  Hell having to cover everyone's PTSD in one mission kind of sucked but could've been done better in many ways.  Maybe actual flashbacks with us operating as the character, and seeing it first hand like we did in BO2.  Speaking of one off missions.  Really, Specter 2, only had one mission and was quick to make one character a traitor.  Someone we didn't even know or "grow" with, and bam he's a bad guy.  At least we had that growth to feel that betrayal in earlier games, so the impact was that much stronger.  So much potential was there, and a lot of implementation that could've made it fun and jaw-dropping.  And yet my hopes were dashed as fast as I knowingly bought the game.  I understand the connection of BO6 and this BO7 heavily requires "the cradle".  So many ideas could come from this bio-weapon, including that it could have originated from the Soviet Union from BO1.  The concept of it being what Alex Mason went through with the brainwashing, but made liquid, similar to what the CIA did with MK-Ultra.  Something that attacks the nervous system fast, and also causes said hallucinations.  But overall the dots are just there and we're barely throwing darts at them to make them stick.  Endgame has some potential, it feels mediocre to me, and wish it was more RPG style with the zones.  Like depending on what you did with friends, by yourself, or operator you choose, you could decrease the effects of the cradle and bring Avalon back to normal.  It's still too early since it's only been what 2-3 days at time of writing.  I don't know what they have planned but, even then this kind of feels mediocre.  Especially a somewhat rogue-like approach where you lose everything if you die, and there is a time limit?  Idk, just me.  Zombies is still too early to tell how it is going to play out, but I played a few games it seems alright, and fun for now.  Hard to mess up zombies but some have in the past or at least messed up maps.  Now for the multiplayer.  I have only played 3 games as of time of writing.  I played one on core, and felt the TTK was weird.  I could lay in a bunch of hits and they wouldn't drop.  Yet they hit me 4 times and the last being a headshot(?), and I'm out.  Played 2 on hard-core.  First match felt off, but still adjusting.  Pace feels stuck between old school boots on the ground, and a little faster due to BO6.  But still somehow slower.  Then my third match.  For some reason they have a fetish for small maps.  I can't remember the name of it, but it was tiny, almost like Babylon tiny.  I got wrecked before I could leave spawn for most of the game.  I am glad that there was a loss forgiveness afterwards, cause we got gobsmacked.  It might be my attachments to my weapons, but my ADS speed felt way too slow, and even though I would fire first, I found myself dead a lot.  I could be ready, ADS, lined up, and just dead.  I know it's me still adjusting but somehow before I could turn a corner, move down a lane, or just anything.  I would be dead.  The pacing just feels stuck.  Stuck between wanting to be proper boots on the ground and absolute crackhead energy we had from BO6.  Even the movement in this game doesn't feel that fluid from the previous game for some reason.  And I only have noticed this from the multiplayer.  Campaign and Endgame felt fine, but Multiplayer just feels like walking through molasses every other step.  I know I'm getting old as well, and my reaction time is slowing down.  But godd*** the pacing feels like sh**.  It really doesn't know what it wants to be.  I know I can and will get better at this, but it just feels like RNG is the name of the game now.  I was hoping overall that this game would almost hit that nostalgia spot that BO2 has.  So much potential was just sh***ed out on the floor and called art.  I'm still going to play this, with regrets.  BO6 was sort of treated too harshly IMO, but there is still some stuff I can nitpick there.  But it realized more of the potential it had than this game did.  Nostalgia can be a game-killer but it also has helped set standards of games for decades.  Please do not waste your money on this immediately, if you get it for free, cool.  If you wait for it to go on sale, wait for the lowest possible price point IMO.  I'm sure some things will get better gameplay wise as they nerf, buff, and update.  But this game has been a big let down so far.  I really only bought this for the campaign since they brought back David and Harper.  But nothing will be the same from when we first started out.

For anyone that actually took the time to read all of this, thank you.  I hope some part of my rant has spoken to you.  I do apologize for how long this review is, but I just was severely disappointed with the game.

Wow, this game is BAD and disgusting.  I have so many grievances with this game and where Triple A games stand.  I thought maybe the use of AI was only only for code but it was for more than that. Co-op Campaign:

The campaign is not like the golden standard of campaigns from previous games.  It is set in a Warzone like map with other people.  It is seperated into combat zones ranging in gear levels. Its all online so there is no pausing and you will get timed out after 15 minutes of pause menu time.  Want to play this offline? The campaign is laughably bad.

Zombies:

Well, there is only one map but this has happened before with Black Ops 2 with Transit.  That map was loved but Shadows of Aether feels souless.  The level design feels like it cannot get a grip what theme it wants directly copying Transit areas.  Every area feels the same in comparison to Transit where each one felt different.  The difficulty is extremely easy as well with large areas to train zombies.  They forced zombies to hit in proximity because of the difficulty and its still very easy.  It felt like I was playing Cold War zombies again not feeling great like a classic zombies experience.  Its just missing the soul it used to have.  Good luck pausing by the way.  15 minute countdown until you are booted off their servers.

Multiplayer:

Black Ops 7 only did one thing good here.  They removed skill based match making and you stay in the lobby after finishing matches.  Its a comeback for Call of Duty... that falls short yet again because of all its blemishes.  The omnidirectional movement feels terrible to combat.  I want to move like in classic Call of Duty where I tell my character to do what it wants.  I turned all movement assists off because I was annoyed I resumed sprinting after moving again when I was just sprinting when I tried to aim.  It persisted and you have to wait for the momentum to stop to walk and aim.  People are constantly slide shotting and being rewarded for it punishing those not using the movement tech. AI Generated content:

I do not support the use of AI in anything because of the way it has been abused.  Real peoples art should be credited and praised.  Black Ops 7 calling cards does something deceptive with its art. Who knows how much else Black Ops 7 used as AI generated help since they do not have to divulge their practices unless any new AI laws attack these deceptive practices.

Verdict:

I do not recommend buying Black Ops 7 at all.  Every mode is a travesty to play and the content of the game has AI generation.  I will not be playing another second of this game. I've absolutely no-lifed this entry so far, reaching Prestige 2 in the second day of the full release, and honestly. I just can't recommend this to anyone. After having played all three modes, let me break down each mode to you and my gripes with it.

Campaign:
Always online, 32 player lobbies (even if you aren't in the "endgame" mode), you'll randomly see people leaving/dying in the match, some people talking in voice chat while you're playing, and more. There's no option to change your difficulty, no ability to pause missions, and despite being focused on a team of four, there are no AI teammates to be there as replacements for the characters not in your party. For some reason despite me not being the party leader I kept being made host of sessions and forced to play as Mason, when you'd expect me to play as a secondary character due to not being host. If you enjoy a chaotic trippy mess it's cool but for a call of duty game it just doesn't hit at all. It seems Black Ops has gone into this loop of "let's take some toxic hallucinogenic gas that causes us to have trippy illusions or dive into the memories and nightmares of another character, and it just doesn't feel right. I explained it to my friend as "this campaign wasn't made for campaign enjoyers, it was made for DMZ/MWZ enjoyers, and that's bad." and that probably sums it up the best way possible.

Multiplayer:
I'm someone who likes to turn my brain off and just shoot stuff in hardcore mode, it's nice to say that you can still do that here! I've already gotten some Dark Ops challenges done such as getting Mega Kill Medals, etc and some games I can do insanely well, getting 80+ kills if I want to, yet other games despite having minimum SBMM I end up in a spawn camped hell. Maybe it's a flaw due to Domination but it feels captured objective focused modes end up with you dying right off rip over and over because the enemies decided to capture two objective and just spawn camp. I've actually seen a game be forfeit due to the enemy team leaving, which I haven't seen since like Modern Warfare 2019?

Zombies:
I am a zombies guy, that's what I hyperfocus on. I already have Bloodstone Camo on my Assault Rifles in the mode (what you'd consider Diamond camo in older games) and honestly, I feel like the Zombies is probably the one mode I have glowing positive remarks about. I have grinded the absolute hell out of it while watching videos or doing other stuff on the side and constantly have ran up 30+ rounds in Survival Vandorn Farm then exfiling without any issues at all. The perks are nice, being able to have an extension to the augments from Black Ops 6 with the ability to equip two minor augments this time instead of one is great and can really make you into a tank, but man this first maps Easter Egg has drained me in solos. I can easily do the steps and make my way to the end boss fight but the final few steps involving shooting a clock tower, running around and doing puzzles, defending 4 artifacts from being destroyed, and then trying to dodge a giant abomination sphere for a boss fight while your main weapon is the Ol' Tessie vehicle it just feels like they really build this Zombies experience around playing with others. Sure, some steps feel easier solo but at the same time it seems the general consensus is "make sure you have gobblegums and perma-perk'd quick revive unlocked if you plan to beat the final boss" due to how unfair he can be for solos players. HOWEVER, This is the longest zombies easter egg in this modern era of Zombies, reminds me of Easter Eggs we'd see like 9 years ago, and it feels good when you actually do get far in it. I just wonder how long until they pull a Black Ops 6 and add weapon bundles to the Store that have built-in elemental mods. Towards the end of BO6 you were able to have Napalm Burst, Dead Wire, and whatever other mod you wanted all on the same gun.

- Multiplayer is multiplayer
- Zombies is basically an improved and expanded Black Ops 6 Zombies

At the time of this review they did reduce the aim assist for controller users so it may take some adjusting. (I use mouse and keyboard) It felt very "loose" so I did have to reduce my dpi. As time goes on I am sure they might balance it a bit more if it becomes intrusive for controller players. For the most part, it feels good. The bullets go where you shoot and register how they should hit. The menu is easy to navigate. You can easily find your missions, unlocks, xp tokens and your player profile. It does not feel like you have to go on a scavenger hunt to find where everything is. 

Please go into your settings and fix to your liking so you can play comfortable. You know your PC system and should already know what you can and can not run properly with your Specs. The game looks and sounds great. You can adjust your settings to make it look better or run smoother. You cant expect a 1080ti to give you 1440p with 165fps. They have a benchmark tool so you can test your settings as well in game. 

If you are having trouble getting kills in game or matching up to other full time players, Call of duty actually made a Non Skill based matchmaking If you want to play casually (btw this is perfectly fine and not an issue).People have been asking for it, cod gave it to them. The Proximity chat and omni movement make it fun to face other players. I played the beta and had such a blast. Everything carried over and what we experienced in the beta is pretty much what we got and then some with the full release. The lobby music of black ops 6 was better IMO but 7 still hits. 

We got a lot of classic maps that were released with the launch as well and they hit the nostalgia factor instantly.

So far, I give the multiplayer aspect of BO7 8/10. 
I will throw this game into my rotation these next few weeks along with arc and bf6. Im not picking this or that one, Ill take them all because of disposable income. Each title releasing around this time has its own fun and drawbacks. Cod is Cod. feels good, runs good. Its a thumbs up for me. There's a lot of about it that I like: perk system is good, attachments feel appropriately varied, it has an advanced stats screen, the SBMM is (currently) less intrusive, the HUD is crisp and clean.. But there's a ton of stuff dragging it down.

As with most new CoDs, the hit reg and lag compensation are atrocious. The spawn system sucks (Idk how they manage to re-botch the spawn system every new release.) The audio is inconsistent and buggy. Hell, even the menu is buggy (I've run into two bugs that I can consistently recreate in-menu, one of which prevents editing perks.) Cheaters are abound atm. Very first match I played had a guy aimbotting with 100% headshots, and have run into more doing the same since.

But even if none of that was a problem, the gameplay (at least the multiplayer) is just.. lackluster. The guns feel.. meh? Mostly not bad, but not great, with a few that feel *really* off. And there isn't very many at launch. The movement feels less floaty than BlOps6, but still floaty, and parts of it are super frenetic while others are super slow. It comes across like it doesn't know what speed it wants the game played at. And the maps all feel super similar, three-lane with a bunch of crisscrossing so you're constantly flankable from tons of angles, which is exacerbated by the bad spawn system.

It's far from the worst a CoD game has been, but I can't recommend it at a $70 price tag. Especially with the technical issues that need fixing. Wait till they've worked on it, and then probably for it to go on sale.

Zombies? Let’s just say I screamed so loud that my neighbor texted to ask if I needed help or if they should also buy the game.

Black Ops 7 is the only game where I paused mid-battle to reflect on my life choices and concluded: “Yes. This is the pinnacle.”

When I think about the worst single-player FPS campaigns I’ve played in the last 25 years, titles like Far Cry New Dawn, Wolfenstein: Youngblood, Halo Infinite, Rage 2, Killzone Shadow Fall, or even Modern Warfare III come to mind. And yet, all of those are masterpieces compared to this soulless abomination disguised as a video game—a product forged in the fires of pure corporate greed.

It has so many baffling design decisions:

- A single-player campaign wrapped in a Warzone-flavored multiplayer shell
- XP and unlocks… in single-player
- No pause button (because who needs basic human functions?)
- Health bars on enemies (aka bullet-sponges)
- Cutscenes. So many cutscenes.
- Packet burst (in a single-player campaign)
- Giant spiders.
- Giant insects.
- A tree made of Frank Woods.
- Wandering through empty Warzone maps while being shot by stationary idiots
- You can’t pick up enemy weapons (a feature that’s worked for two decades—gone!)
- Completely chaotic tone: cyborgs, zombies, ninjas, soldiers… all in the first 20 minutes
- A boss fight in those same 20 minutes—only winnable with killstreaks
- Trippy hallucination sequences (the part nobody likes, but they keep doing anyway)
- Invisible teammates because… it’s secretly a co-op campaign for some reason
- UI straight out of a mobile game
- And overall the vibe of “no one talked to anyone and we shipped it anyway”

Game's been out for ten days, so I'm updating my review, now that I've gotten a number of hours played under my belt. It's pretty terrible, all things considered. The "Co-Op Campaign" is not a traditional Call of Duty Campaign as you've come to expect, it's what effectively amounts to 11 Spec-Ops mission, all strung together by minor gameplay sequences on the open-world map in which it takes place. Yes, the entire thing is forcibly online, it has matchmaking that does not scale missions down in enemy density when disabled, and you cannot pause or save your progress. That all sucks. The "Endgame" mode that they keep advertising is basically the DMZ mode from Modern Warfare II/III several years ago, with nothing really different.

The multiplayer is basically the exact same thing you played 10 years ago when Black Ops 3 came out. "Omni-movement" creates a drastic skill gap in public matches, shotguns are busted, snipers are busted, they added the ability to see and kill enemy players through walls as a scorestreak, and the maps all have the same three-lane design you know and hate. You'll get matchmade with people who are already Prestige Level 5, and will run around no-scoping people or diving into people with a knife, then flame you in chat afterwards. Awful experience all-around.

Now, for the reason I really got this game: Zombies. It's...fun? The only current map, Ashes of the Damned, is conceptually interesting. It feels like an evolution of the Outbreak mode from Black Ops Cold War if you ever played that, and Tranzit from Black Ops 2. I have attempted the Main Quest (Easter Egg) more than 15 times, got to the final boss, and failed. The problem with this game is that it feels as though it was coded by a team of 4 or 5 interns using ChatGPT Model 1 to do all their programming for them. The questline is the longest in franchise history, which makes the "walk-back" after every failed attempt feel excruciating, and the difficulty scaling throughout is absolutely horrid. It's incredibly buggy too, not to mention, DirectX API errors and resulting game crashes galore, glitching through the map boundary and being forced to reset, being randomly killed by the game in-between rounds, getting one-hit killed by zombies through all your perks and armor vest...it's a mess. Just about none of my deaths feel deserved, and that's an awful feeling.

If you're at all interested in playing this game, it should be for the Zombies mode and nothing else. With that said, wait a couple months for it to be like 50% off. By then, many of these bugs and tuning issues should be fixed, and there should be more content to play from. It could also get worse...you never know with this company anymore.

I don’t think the $70 price tag for BO7 is inherently unjustified, that’s the new normal in gaming. But just because $70 is standard doesn’t mean BO7 actually earns that value. And honestly? It doesn’t.

The campaign is unbelievably weak, multiplayer feels undercooked, and Zombies is… fine, but painfully underwhelming. I wanted to love Ashes of the Damned, and while I did enjoy parts of it, the map ultimately feels “meh.” There’s nothing new to set it apart from its predecessor. 

The return of the original four should have been a big moment, but instead they’re pulled from random timelines with no cohesion, and Takeo’s voice actor change feels completely off. And the bear boss? Probably the most annoying map-specific boss Zombies has ever had.

What’s sad is that COD is becoming something I play alone now. Not because I’m antisocial, but because nobody I know wants to play it anymore. Before BO7 launched, I asked ten people if they were excited — eight said, “What’s that?” and the other two said no. The hype is gone. The social aspect is gone. Unless you’re a diehard or a content creator, the franchise just doesn’t seem to hold people anymore.

Maybe BO7 will pull a MW3 and 
improve dramatically over time, but honestly that feels like cope. And things like AI calling cards make it even worse. It’s like the focus is everywhere except where players actually need it to be.
I’m not asking for miracles. I just want COD to feel like COD again. 

Give us meaningful updates. Give Zombies some real innovation. Give multiplayer a pulse. Stop pushing cosmetic fluff while the core experience struggles.
